subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add workspace-wide editing and any host/system filesystem browser scope to Mission Control, and what authorization boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: Current source shows the remaining gap, but the request changes which local files operator clients can read or write and crosses a security boundary that current main only extends for read-only workspace previews.

options.title: Approve Workspace-Only Next Step
options.body: Keep host/system browsing out of this issue and route workspace browsing/editing through a bounded `agents.workspace` design with read/admin scopes, root confinement, limits, destructive-operation UX, and real UI proof.

options.title: Keep Bootstrap-Only Editing
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing restricted to bootstrap and memory files while allowing separate read-only workspace previews for inspection.

options.title: Open System Scope Design
options.body: Require a separate security design for host filesystem browsing with explicit opt-in, auditing, sensitive-file handling, and read/write limits before implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace-Only Next Step
recommendation.body: Keep host/system browsing out of this issue and route workspace browsing/editing through a bounded `agents.workspace` design with read/admin scopes, root confinement, limits, destructive-operation UX, and real UI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current read-only workspace RPC boundary and mobile Files landing, making them the best current routing candidate for the next scope decision.
